source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: Derrick White
injuries.short_comment: White (shoulder) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Sacramento.
injuries.long_comment: White drew the questionable tag for Saturday's game due to left AC joint sprain in his shoulder. The veteran guard will be in street clothes for the first leg of the Celtics' back-to-back set, but he could make his return Sunday against the Warriors. With Jayson Tatum (rest) also out, Payton Pritchard and Paul George will carry the workload for the Celtics, and there will be more opportunities for the likes of Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh.

injuries.name: Jayson Tatum
injuries.short_comment: Tatum (rest) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Kings.
injuries.long_comment: Tatum will be rested for the first leg of the Celtics' back-to-back set, so he should be back on the floor for Sunday's game against the Warriors. With both Tatum and Derrick White (shoulder) sidelined, the Celtics will rely more heavily on Paul George, Payton Pritchard, Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Sam Hauser to carry the scoring load against Sacramento.

injuries.name: Mitchell Robinson
injuries.short_comment: Robinson (illness) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Kings, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
injuries.long_comment: Robinson is under the weather and will not play in the front end of Boston's back-to-back set, but he could be available for Sunday night's game against the Warriors. With Robinson sidelined, Luka Garza and Chris Cenac should both see a bump in minutes behind starting center Neemias Queta.

injuries.name: Kristaps Porzingis
injuries.short_comment: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
injuries.long_comment: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

injuries.name: Stephen Curry
injuries.short_comment: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long_comment: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

injuries.name: Brandon Williams
injuries.short_comment: Williams (hamstring) is out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
injuries.long_comment: Williams recently progressed to on-court work, but he will remain on the inactive list for Sunday's game. His next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Kings.

injuries.name: Moses Moody
injuries.short_comment: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injuries.long_comment: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

injuries.name: Jimmy Butler III
injuries.short_comment: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injuries.long_comment: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.
